status: re-collected and re-extracted 2026-08-30; award recovered; video tier collected; community tier still missing
note: Method lives in .claude/skills/consensus-guide/SKILL.md. This file records what is specific to fish and chips: the one national award, the fact that it publishes no results, and the two sources that were recorded while contributing nothing.

awardBodies.name: National Fish and Chip Awards
awardBodies.note: Run by the National Federation of Fish Friers. Judged, dated, ceremony each February. 14 categories; Takeaway of the Year runs Top 40 -> Top 20 -> Top 10 -> winner.
awardBodies.readTheResultsElsewhere: THE AWARDS BODY PUBLISHES NO RESULTS PAGE. thefishandchipawards.com carries entry information, category descriptions and a scatter of 2023 shortlist posts; there is no winners page and nothing in its sitemap for 2026. But the PARENT federation does publish some of it: nfff.co.uk/let-the-batter-commence/ (13 Nov 2025) names the ten Takeaway of the Year finalists. So the 40-shop shortlist comes from Time Out's report and the 10-shop final from the federation itself. ATTRIBUTE BOTH TO THE AWARD - filing a national award under timeout.com collapses it into a masthead that already counts here.
awardBodies.londonEntries2026: Two of forty on the shortlist: Brockley's Rock (Brockley) and Stones Fish and Chips (Acton). Only Brockley's Rock made the final ten, and it is the only London shop in it. Stones was also a UK top-three finalist in Marketing Initiative and in Training and Development, winning neither.
awardBodies.openQuestion: The February 2026 ceremony has happened and the Takeaway of the Year winner is on neither site. Checked both sitemaps on 2026-08-30. Worth one more look next refresh.

awardBodies.name: Fry magazine UK top 50
awardBodies.note: NOT COLLECTED. The trade magazine ran a UK top 50 in 2024 - Stones Fish and Chips is named in it via Time Out - but fry-magazine.com does not resolve and no archive of the list was found. Left out rather than reconstructed.

editorialLists.name: Time Out
editorialLists.note: RANKED 1-18 and its ranking disagrees sharply with the citation counts - Michael's Fish Bar in Leytonstone is its #1 and carries only two sources, while Poppies is the most-cited chippy in the corpus and is not on Time Out's list at all. Ranks and per-venue text recorded 2026-08-30; the first pass captured the page heading as a venue and kept neither.

editorialLists.name: Absolutely
editorialLists.note: Six of its twenty captured names were section headings and footer links ('Top Eats', 'Topics', 'Other Absolutely Titles').

editorialLists.name: British Food Crew
editorialLists.note: Captured its own site furniture as venues, including an emoji heading.

editorialLists.name: Travelicious Bites
editorialLists.note: Four of ten captured names were footer links (Gigs, Explore, Company, Cookie Preferences).

editorialLists.name: James Dimitri
editorialLists.note: The longest single list in the corpus at 35 shops, and the only one that reaches outside London - Molesey Fish Bar is in Surrey and Marlow Fish Bar in Buckinghamshire. Both are recorded in data/name-noise.json under outOfArea.

facetAxis.note: Fish and chips splits by FORMAT and by FRYING MEDIUM. Format decides the price and the evening; the medium is the one technical fact regulars actually argue about, and almost no guide prints it.

knownGaps: COMMUNITY TIER IS EMPTY. No Reddit or forum threads. Reddit is blocked to curl and to the browser pane, and two Apify runs on other topics cost about $0.95 for nothing usable.
ONLY TWO VENUES CARRY A DATED AWARD, and both are shortlist places rather than wins. The award publishes no results, so even the win cannot be recorded.

The corpus leans C-tier. Six of thirteen sources are independent blogs and specialists rather than mastheads, which is unusual for this project and reflects how little the big titles cover chippies outside a once-a-year listicle.
Fry magazine's UK top 50 is a real second award and could not be read - the domain does not resolve.

videoTier.method: Apify api-ninja/youtube-search-scraper, videoDepthDetails=standard, geo=GB. Names read from YouTube's own chapter markers, so no handle was reconstructed. Cost about $0.002.
videoTier.rejected: Nine channels named nothing extractable, covered the UK rather than London, or anonymised their chapters ('The Soho One', 'The Wildcard'). A channel with no extractable venue is not a source.
videoTier.warning: RestroSpot's chapter markers are AUTO-GENERATED FROM SPEECH and come back mangled - 'Toss' for Toff's, 'Falers' for Faulkners, 'Sutton Suns' for Sutton & Sons. Only unambiguous names were recorded; the rest were dropped rather than guessed at.

openVenueQuestions: Two shops named Kennedy's trade in London and the group itself is 'Kennedy's London' with five branches. The one in the corpus is the Goswell Road chippy named in a video chapter marker; its row is slugged kennedys-goswell-road.
The Golden Chippy (Greenwich) and The Golden Chip of Hanwell are different businesses with near-identical names, recorded in data/name-aliases.json under deliberatelyNotAliased.

SEVENTEEN IS UNRESOLVED AND HAS NO ROW. Three London businesses trade as some form of the name: a CHINESE restaurant at 17 Notting Hill Gate, Seventeen Fish Bar in Whetstone N20, and the one the sources appear to mean - a modern chippy on Chestnut Grove in Balham, per Cozymeal, with the Instagram handle Absolutely gives. Only one source states a street, no website was reachable, and a pinned marker on a guessed address puts a reader outside the wrong building. Named in the article's closing table with that caveat, and left off the map.
Hobson's is THREE branches - Porchester Road W2, St Anne's Court W1F, and Villiers Street WC2N off the Strand. Secondary listings place it on Charing Cross ROAD and in Victoria; both are wrong.
Fishcotheque's trading status could not be confirmed from a primary source - its apparent domain has expired. Its own social page and dated third-party reviews suggest it is open. The row says so.
Oliver's Whetstone branch has closed; only Belsize Park trades. Its own site and its menu PDF disagree on Sunday opening.
